hypothesis: Starting from the iteration-2 configuration (h_px=1.5) and making the scratch detector more sensitive (scratch_min_contrast 0.10->0.07, scratch_min_length_px 200->140) will do three things. (1) scratch_recall_crossing will rise from 0.70 to >= 0.80, with scratch_precision falling by <= 0.10. (2) Laths will be cut less often by un-inpainted scratch remnants, so median_aspect_ratio_bias improves by >= 0.03 in weak_harsh (-0.139 -> >= -0.11) and in moderate_scratched (image 1: -0.145 -> >= -0.115). worst_family_tolerance_ratio falls from 0.93 to <= 0.85. (3) Clean-family AR bias moves by <= 0.02 and direction/S ratios move by <= 0.02. If crossing recall rises by >= 0.08 but harsh AR bias moves by < 0.03, missed scratches are not the main cause of the shortened flakes; noise ridges are then the next suspect.
review_reason:
The run passes the automatic check, but it refutes the hypothesis. The pooled worst_tolerance_ratio of 0.32 meets the target only because pooling hides the bad family; the worst family is 0.935, which is not an improvement.

Pre-registered predictions against results:
- (1) Crossing scratch recall: 0.70 -> 0.750, short of the >= 0.80 target. Precision stayed at 0.95, so the cost was small, but the gain is half the predicted size.
- (2) Aspect-ratio bias: unchanged everywhere. weak_harsh stays at -0.140 (target >= -0.11). moderate_scratched_1 is -0.145, exactly as before. worst_family_tolerance_ratio is 0.93 -> 0.935, against a target of <= 0.85.
- (3) Clean families barely moved, as predicted. moderate_clean_2 still has 1066 false scratch pixels.

The per-image data rule out the scratch-miss explanation for the worst family:
- Both weak_harsh images already have about 95% crossing recall (10693/11278 and 10289/10732) and no parallel scratches. Yet their AR bias is -0.136 and -0.144.
- weak_scratched has much lower recall (0.43 and 0.85) and only about -0.03 bias.
- So missed scratches are not what shortens the flakes in weak_harsh. The 'harsh' condition is, i.e. noise ridges or contrast. A third possibility is that detected-and-masked scratches are themselves acting as cut lines: weak_harsh has about 16k scratch px versus 4-6k in weak_scratched.
- Neither pre-registered branch fires cleanly, because recall rose only 0.05, not 0.08. The data still point the same way as the fallback branch.
- n=2 per family, so family numbers are weak. The per-image pattern is consistent across both weak_harsh images, though.

What the overlays show:
- moderate_scratched_1: one detected scratch (left, about (220,365)-(0,640)) is dashed and broken. Recall on this image is only 0.54. A pink elongated region along the colony boundary (about x 390-660, y 155-205) and an orange sliver at the right edge (about 990,420) look like grain-boundary alpha counted as flakes.
- random_harsh_0: crossing recall is 0.51. The left scratch (0,560)-(415,520) stops at about x 415. The near-vertical scratch (290,610)-(390,330) is fragmented. The short white segment at about (500,370)-(525,400) may be a false or partial detection.
- strong_harsh_0: flake recall is 0.72. A large share of laths are grey, i.e. excluded, and fragmented. Several beaded grey lines run near-parallel to the laths and are not detected, consistent with parallel recall of 111/3436 = 3%. I did not see an obvious colony boundary drawn white.

Other problems:
- The pooled flake_recall still equals moderate_clean exactly, so the evaluator bug is unfixed.
- Real Ti-6Al-4V and the rotation self-consistency test remain untested.

Confidence that the scratch-sensitivity lever is not the main AR fix: about 80%.
next_step:
Run a diagnostic before any further tuning, keeping h_px=1.5, scratch_min_contrast=0.07 and scratch_min_length_px=140. The recall gain was cheap, so keep those values. Add to the evaluator, per image:
- the fraction of predicted flake ends within 3 px of the detected scratch mask;
- the fraction within 3 px of the true scratch mask;
- the fraction within 3 px of neither, which points to noise ridges.
If possible, also run once with the ground-truth scratch mask in place of the detected one on the harsh and scratched families.

How to read the outcome:
- If AR bias stays at about -0.14 with the true mask, scratches are not the cause and noise ridges are. Then raise the ridge/Sato response threshold or sigma (exposing the parameter if needed) and test on weak_harsh only.
- If ends cluster at detected scratches, no existing parameter fixes it. The method needs a scratch-aware merge step: rejoin collinear fragments across the inpainted scratch strip when the orientation difference is < 5 deg and the lateral offset is < half a lath width.
- Parallel scratches still need a new global Hough/RANSAC line step.

Also fix the pooled flake_recall bug, and implement the 30/60/90 deg rotation self-consistency test on the real Ti-6Al-4V images.
rationale:
What is known from iterations 1 and 2:
- Aspect ratio is the binding term, and it is biased negative, meaning flakes are cut short.
- Raising h_px barely moved the weak_harsh AR bias (about 0.01, below the pre-registered 0.03). So watershed over-splitting is not the main cause.
- Every unscratched image has AR bias near 0 (-0.04 to +0.07). Every scratched image is negative, and the worst images are the scratch-heavy ones.
- About 30% of crossing-scratch pixels go undetected. The overlays show scratches detected only as dashed lines or stopping partway, with faint continuations left in place. An undetected scratch is not inpainted. The Sato ridge filter then sees it as a dark line across the laths and cuts them there. That fits the negative, scratch-correlated bias.

Why this lever and not others:
- The reviewer suggested bridge_gaps_px of about 8-10, but the default is already 9, so that is not a real change.
- bridge_gaps_px also closes gaps along the laths and cannot remove a full cross-cut.
- merge_saddle_ratio cannot rejoin pieces separated by a complete boundary line.
- So scratch sensitivity is the lever that tests the scratch explanation directly.
- It also attacks a requirement of the research question that is currently unmet: crossing recall >= 0.9 and scratches kept from cutting flakes.

Design:
- h_px stays at 1.5, so iteration 2 is the baseline and the only change is the two scratch-sensitivity thresholds, varied together as one lever.
- Guards: false scratch pixels on clean images, especially moderate_clean_2, which already has 1066 false px; clean-family AR bias; scratch_precision.
- The colony-boundary safeguards (scratch_max_side_diff_deg, continuity) are left at default, so grain boundaries should still be kept.
- Each family has only n=2 images, so I will read per-image AR bias and not over-interpret family changes below about 0.1.

Confidence: about 40% that AR improves as predicted; about 60% that crossing recall reaches >= 0.80.

What this run cannot do:
- Parallel scratches (recall 0.055) still need a new global Hough/RANSAC line step that accepts lines continuing across colony boundaries.
- Real Ti-6Al-4V is still untested. It needs a new rotation self-consistency method: rotate each image by 30, 60 and 90 degrees, rerun flakes with fixed params, and report the direction deviation and the changes in S and aspect ratio.
- A useful extra diagnostic would be the fraction of flake ends within 3 px of a detected or true scratch, per image.
- The pooled flake_recall reporting bug (it equals moderate_clean exactly) should be fixed in the evaluator.
